new_papers.title: REMem: Reasoning with Episodic Memory in Language Agent
key_findings: Two-phase framework for episodic memory: indexing (converts experiences into hybrid memory graph linking time-aware gists and facts) and agentic inference (agentic retriever with curated tools for iterative retrieval over memory graph)
Achieves 3.4% and 13.4% absolute improvements on episodic recollection and reasoning tasks vs. Mem0 and HippoRAG 2
Only method to exceed 90% exact match on Test of Time benchmark
More robust refusal behavior for unanswerable questions

new_papers.title: Structural Hallucination in Large Language Models: A Network-Based Evaluation of Knowledge Organization and Citation Integrity
key_findings: Introduces 'structural hallucination': systematic distortion of conceptual organization, relational architecture, and bibliographic grounding invisible to sentence-level metrics
Network-based stress test: knowledge graph extraction, graph similarity analysis, centrality comparison, citation integrity verification
Three benchmarks: Roget's Thesaurus (lexical ontology), Wikidata philosophers (biographical KG), Dimensions.ai citations (bibliometric)
Roget: macro-F1 < 0.05, node-set Jaccard 0.028, 94.3% node fabrication rate
Wikidata: hallucination rates exceed 93% in biographical benchmark
Bibliometric: citation omission reaches 91.9%
Structural fidelity cannot be inferred from local fluency alone

new_papers.title: Learning What to Remember: A Cognitively Grounded Multi-Factor Value Model for Agentic Memory
authors: (authors from search result - need to verify)
key_findings: Multi-factor memory value function with seven interpretable factors: emotional intensity, goal relevance, value alignment, self/user relevance, task utility, reliability, usage history
Single scalar uniformly drives encoding depth, forgetting, and retrieval
Separates consolidation-time (no query) from retrieval-time (query exists) decision regimes
Learned multi-factor value retains gold-standard memories far better than single-factor baselines (similarity, recency) at consolidation time

new_papers.title: Experience Memory Graph: One-Shot Error Correction for Agents
key_findings: Reformulates agent failure recovery as graph matching problem
Converts failed and successful trajectories into directed action decision graphs at training time
Extracts common subgraphs (successful workflows) and graph edit paths (corrective actions for failures)
At test time: retrieves relevant insights and guides agent in single loop-free execution
Outperforms reflection baselines on ALFWorld and ScienceWorld in success rate and average reward
No test-time trial-and-error required

new_papers.title: MemoryForge: Synthesize Lifelong Memory for Human-Like LLM Agents
key_findings: Memory-based conditioning paradigm: replaces abstract profiles with autobiographical memory base
Formalizes customized lifelong memory synthesis: given brief persona description, produce memory base spanning full developmental trajectory
Multi-resolution simulator generates specific experiences, general events, life periods from brief persona
Enables frozen LLMs to dynamically retrieve situation-relevant memory for behavior guidance
Addresses limitations of trait labels and scripted dialogues by grounding dispositions in accumulated experiences

new_papers.title: Rethinking Memory as Continuously Evolving Connectivity
key_findings: FluxMem: connectivity-evolving memory framework modeling memory as heterogeneous graph
Three stages: initial connection formation, feedback-driven refinement, long-term consolidation
During execution: repairs missing links, prunes interference, aligns abstraction granularity, distills recurrent successful trajectories into reusable procedural circuits
Guided by metric for memory generalizability and evolutionary maturity
Memory emerges as self-organizing structure where units and connections continuously adapt and evolve

new_papers.title: Worth Remembering: Surprise-Gated Robot Episodic Memory
key_findings: Episodic memory system for robotics using Bayesian surprise of V-JEPA-2 latent space embeddings
Selectively stores high-utility experiences during long-horizon (>30 min) robot rollouts
Surprise gate is causal, unsupervised, augments 4D scene graph (DAAAM) with generically useful events
Robust threshold (median absolute deviation) on surprise signal gates which frames stored as episodic traces

new_papers.title: EMBER: Autonomous Cognitive Behaviour from Learned Spiking Neural Network Dynamics in a Hybrid LLM Architecture
key_findings: Reorganizes LLM-memory relationship: LLM as replaceable reasoning engine, associative memory in biologically-grounded SNN substrate
Associations learned through STDP (spike-timing-dependent plasticity), expressed through lateral propagation
Three complementary stores: episodic memory (temporal sequences replayed for testing effect), perfect recall (exact fact storage), personal journal (system's own reflections)
Consolidation follows complementary learning systems theory: fast hippocampal learning + slow cortical learning with interleaved replay

new_papers.title: Persona Without Substrate: Regime-Dependence and the LLM Individuation Problem
key_findings: Addresses LLM individuation problem: when we speak of 'the LLM', what exactly do we refer to? (weights, virtual instance, persona region, model-level character)
Uses mechanistic interpretability results (Anthropic's persona vectors, Persona Selection Model, Assistant Axis, emergent misalignment) as empirical ground for ontological argument
Reveals tacit commitment in persona-vectors literature that 'persona vector' picks out same content-bearing object across elicitation regimes
Challenges this commitment showing regime-dependence of persona attribution

new_papers.title: Reality Monitoring in Large Language Models: Self-Knowledge That Transforms with Conversation Memory
key_findings: Adapts reality monitoring (RM) framework from human cognitive psychology to assess source monitoring in LLMs
Word-pair task: LLMs encode pairs with second word externally provided (perceived) or internally generated (imagined), then attribute source
Ceiling accuracy for self-generated content under minimal memory demands reverses to fragile external-item advantage once episodic delay removes shortcut
Feedback exposes failures: internal/external judgments swap, or accuracy improves while confidence decouples from correctness
RM failures associated with hallucinations/delusions in schizophrenia; conceptually adjacent to LLM hallucinations

new_papers.title: PsychoAgent: An Affect-Sensitive Cognitive Architecture for Conflict-Aware Memory in LLM Agents
key_findings: Separates factual and affective memory, integrates both through conflict-aware executive controller
Affective memories filtered by semantic relevance then re-ranked by salience, preserving topical fit while allowing emotionally important traces
Three-day trace shows persistent affect, offline memory recombination, selective memory reweighting
Supports affect-sensitive retrieval as inspectable mechanism for modeling human-like conflict effects

new_papers.title: Always-On Agents: A Survey of Persistent Memory, State, and Governance in LLM Agents
key_findings: Comprehensive survey of persistent-state systems (always-on agents) including retrievable memories, task ledgers, permissions, credentials, commitments, provenance, audit records, shared state, trigger conditions, externally committed effects
Five adjacent system classes: agentic databases, agent OS, LLM serving runtimes, orchestration frameworks, capability security
Covers multimodal memory, agentic-OS/serving runtimes, systems cost and resource governance, cross-substrate synthesis

new_papers.title: MemoryCPT: An End-to-End Agent Memory Framework for Cost-Performance Trade-off
key_findings: End-to-end trainable agent memory pipeline spanning offline memory construction and online query-conditioned context generation
Query-aware Retrieval and Summarization (QAR): reciprocal rank fusion (RRF) + LoRA-based summarizer trained via GRPO under cost-aware reward
Introduces Quality per Cost (QPC) metric for answer quality per unit inference cost
Improves cost-performance trade-off on LoCoMo and LongMemEval

new_papers.title: Beyond Semantic Organization: Memory as Execution State Management for Long-Horizon Agents
key_findings: Mage: active execution-state manager storing interactions in hierarchical state tree
Agent derives state from active root-to-current path combining subgoal summaries, recent traces, hints from prior branches
Four coupled operations: Grow (records new traces), Compress (summarizes completed subgoals), Maintain (validates summaries), Revise (restores target boundary and resumes on new branch)
Shifts memory from similarity-driven archive to execution-state manager for interdependent long-horizon tasks

new_papers.title: NeurOWL: An LLM-Based Neural-symbolic Framework for Incomplete OWL Ontology Reasoning
key_findings: End-to-end neuro-symbolic framework for explainable subsumption reasoning over incomplete OWL ontologies
Jointly performs verification and abduction: identifies meaningful missing components compatible with existing information
Operates in training-free and fine-tuned settings, adapts across domains
Iteratively recovers subset- and entailment-minimal solutions as missing axioms
Evaluated on FoodOn, Gene Ontology, SNOMED CT with F1 scores 0.893-0.970

new_papers.title: OntoTKGE: Ontology-Enhanced Temporal Knowledge Graph Extrapolation
key_findings: Integrates ontological knowledge into temporal KG extrapolation via CompGCN entity/concept embeddings
Feeds ontology-enhanced embeddings into TKG extrapolation model encoder at first timestamp
Enables entity embedding prediction at timestamp t+1 with ontological grounding

new_papers.title: Better Later Than Sooner: Neuro-Symbolic Knowledge Graph Construction via Ontology-grounded Post-extraction Correction
key_findings: Neuro-symbolic framework for ontology-grounded KG construction: open-domain extraction, embedding-based canonicalization, targeted LLM-based correction of ontology violations
Defers corrections to post-extraction stage, avoiding repeated LLM calls
OAK+MEND method: improves ontology consistency of triples from 63.4% to 96.8% (Qwen3-30B-A3B) and 67.9% to 98.4% (GPT-OSS-120B)
Qualifiers: 33.6% to 91.5% (Qwen) and 35.7% to 96.8% (GPT-OSS)
More token efficient than in-context and Wikontic baselines (59-79% of Wikontic cost)
Introduces SPARQL graph-patterns benchmark for symbolic querying evaluation

new_papers.title: NeuroSymActive: Differentiable Neural-Symbolic Reasoning with Active Exploration for Knowledge Graph Question Answering
key_findings: Modular framework: differentiable neural-symbolic reasoning layer + neural path evaluator + Monte-Carlo active exploration controller
Soft-unification style symbolic modules with differentiable rule scoring
Neural path evaluator assigns value estimates to partial reasoning trajectories
Active exploration prioritizes high-value path expansions, reduces expensive KG queries
Two coupled loops: inner (fast differentiable neural-symbolic exploration) and outer (human oracle queries when uncertainty exceeds threshold)
Gumbel-Softmax relaxations for end-to-end differentiability

new_papers.title: CORTEX: High-Quality Cross-Domain Organization of Web-Scale Corpora through Ontological Corpus Graph
key_findings: Ontological Corpus Graph (OCG): three-layer heterogeneous structure unifying quality-refined content layer, hierarchical lightweight ontology layer (LLM-driven automated evolution), cross-domain alignment layer
Enables inter-domain association at arbitrary taxonomic resolution via Typicality-Fidelity-Specificity (TFS) weighted linkages
Evaluated across eight frontier LLMs validating quality refinement, domain organization, cross-domain data synthesis
Public release: 24.14B-token refined corpus with OCG and CortexBench

new_papers.title: gUFO: A Gentle Foundational Ontology for Semantic Web Knowledge Graphs
key_findings: Lightweight implementation of Unified Foundational Ontology (UFO) for OWL 2 DL applications
Unique support for typology of types (operationalizing OntoClean guidelines), reification patterns for intrinsic/relational aspects, situations and high-order types
51 classes, 40 object properties, 7 data properties
Two disjoint taxonomies: Taxonomy of Individuals (Object, Quality, Situation, Event) and Taxonomy of Types (Kind, Phase, Role, Category)
Explicit support for temporary instantiation/parthood/relationship situations addressing temporal problem in OWL 2 DL
UFO in process of ISO/IEC standardization as CD 21838-5

new_papers.title: The Missing Knowledge Layer in AI: A Framework for Stable Human-AI Reasoning
key_findings: Argues humans systematically under-track uncertainty and conflate inference with fact (structural feature of cognition)
LLMs inherit this cognitive vulnerability: epistemic markers sparse/implicit/inconsistent in training data

Structural absence explains patterned LLM failures: hallucinations = unrecognized transitions from grounded retrieval to speculative interpolation; overconfidence = undifferentiated surface confidence; false coherence = linguistically smooth but internally unstable trajectories
Improving factual accuracy, scaling capacity, or more training data does not resolve underlying epistemic representation problem

new_papers.title: Generative Ontology: When Structured Knowledge Learns to Create
key_findings: Introduces Generative Ontology framework synthesizing ontology (grammar) and LLM (creativity)
Traditional ontologies passive (describe what exists); LLMs generate fluently but lack structural validity
Structural hallucination in creative domains: LLMs generate appearance of game designs without substance (mechanisms without components, goals without end conditions)
Ontology provides grammar for valid generation; LLM provides creativity within structural constraints

new_papers.title: Nested Episodic State Topology (NEST): A Graph-Theoretic Architecture of Cognitive States
key_findings: Graph-theoretic representational ontology modeling cognition as structured state formation
Six relation types: causal, containment, temporal, associative, evidential, spatial
Typed, weighted graphs where nodes may carry subgraph payloads
Separates durable belief graphs from capacity-limited working-memory graphs
Formal belief-update operators and conflict catalogs
Maps multiple cognitive architectures (ACT-R, Soar, Sigma, Global Workspace Theory, chunking) as constrained regions of one unified language

new_papers.title: Human-Like Lifelong Memory: A Neuroscience-Grounded Architecture for Infinite Interaction
key_findings: Integrates 12 principles from cognitive neuroscience and clinical psychology into computational mechanisms
Dual-store architecture: capacity-limited working memory buffer + persistent knowledge graph (hippocampal-neocortical complementary learning systems)
CBT-inspired belief hierarchy for identity (core/intermediate/automatic thoughts as weighted gists)
System 1/2 retrieval routing with epistemic self-awareness, curiosity-driven gist formation, identity persistence
Thalamic gateway tags and routes information between stores
Reconsolidation via cathartic modification (not append-only)
Converges toward System 1 processing over time (computational analog of clinical expertise)

new_papers.title: OG-MAR: Ontology-Grounded Multi-Agent Reasoning
key_findings: Framework using ontology to surface right personas and assemble them into multi-agent system
Combines ontology and multi-agent systems for grounded reasoning
From Enhans research group (Wonduk Seo)

new_papers.title: SPIO: Ensemble and Selective Strategies via LLM-based Multi-Agent Planning in Automated Data Science
key_findings: Multi-agent framework where LLMs build memory over time and use it to construct full data science scenarios
Goes beyond simple code generation to memory-augmented multi-agent planning

new_papers.title: StructHallu-Drift: Benchmarking Structured Hallucinations Under Schema Evolution in LLMs
key_findings: Six-category hallucination taxonomy disentangling syntactic validity from semantic fidelity
Controlled evaluation suite applying realistic schema mutations at three severity levels to NL-to-structure datasets
1,200 schema-model evaluation instances across 4 LLMs (7B-70B) and 3 structured output tasks

Key findings: 39-54% of structured outputs contain semantic hallucination; schema drift severity has minimal effect (~44% across levels, p=0.59); output format dominant factor (SQL ~85% semantic validity vs schema-grounded records 7-24%); each model has distinct hallucination fingerprint

new_papers.title: Why LLMs Hallucinate on Structured Knowledge: A Mechanistic Analysis of Reasoning over Linearized Representations
key_findings: Two mechanistic signals: Structural Shortcut Reliance (SSR) - attention over-concentrates on shortcut-like structural cues; Semantic Alignment Score (SAS) - FFN representations fail to maintain semantic grounding, revert to parametric memory
SSR varies with task complexity/format; SAS more stable role in mitigating hallucination
Lightweight hallucination detector based on SSR/SAS outperforms confidence/consistency baselines without model modification
Generalizes beyond single-hop to multi-hop graphs and tabular settings

new_papers.title: EMA: An Episodic Memory Agent for Efficient and Selective Memory
key_findings: Episodic Memory Units (EMUs) abstract conversational context with event content, time/location, participants, subjective importance
MemDecider filtering decision module for selective retention
Competitive performance on LoCoMo and Long-MT-Bench+ while reducing token usage by 11.48% average

new_papers.title: Reasoning with Ontology Graph: Toward Type-Constrained Knowledge Graph Question Answering
key_findings: Planner-judge architecture with generative backoff: type planner proposes head-tail type pairs, judge verifies candidates/paths, generator invoked only when all candidates rejected
Type-constrained reasoning: constrains both endpoints in type space
SOTA on WebQSP (87.7%→91.5% Hit@1) and CWQ (67.6%→74.6% Hit@1)
Produces ontology-grounded reasoning chains

new_papers.title: SymAgent: A Neural-Symbolic Self-Learning Agent Framework for Complex Reasoning over Knowledge Graphs
key_findings: Neural-symbolic agent with Agent-Planner (extracts symbolic rules from KG for question decomposition) and Agent-Executor (invokes action tools for KG + external documents)
Treats KG as dynamic environment, transforms reasoning into multi-step interactive process
Self-learning framework: online exploration + offline iterative policy updating
Identifies missing triples facilitating automatic KG updates
Weak LLM backbones (7B) achieve better/comparable performance to strong baselines

new_papers.title: Memory Is Reconstructed, Not Retrieved: Graph Memory for LLM Agents
new_papers.venue: ICLR 2026 Workshop on Memory for LLM-Based Agentic Systems (MemAgents)
key_findings: MRAgent: associative memory graph (Cue-Tag-Content) with active reconstruction mechanism
Associative tags as semantic bridges connecting fine-grained cues to memory contents
Integrates LLM reasoning directly into memory access, iteratively explores/prunes retrieval paths
Up to 23% improvement on LoCoMo and LongMemEval, substantially reducing token/runtime cost

new_papers.title: Knowledge Reasoning Language Model: Unifying Knowledge and Language for Inductive Knowledge Graph Reasoning
key_findings: KRLM: unifies LLM knowledge with KG context for inductive KGR
Knowledge Reasoning Language (KRL) instruction format and KRL tokenizer to align LLM knowledge with KG representations
KRL attention layer coordinates intrinsic LLM knowledge with KG context via dynamic knowledge memory mechanism
Structure-aware next-entity predictor constrains reasoning within trustworthy knowledge domain
SOTA on 25 real-world inductive KGR datasets in zero-shot and fine-tuning
